tube.why: five wide and five high, as the Rift dig camp's adit (data/rift_mines.json features adit): room to ride a Pokemon down 1.3 km of drift

shell_why: every cell within 2 of anything carved, and at or under the ground, is written as rock, so the drift is bounded only by blocks this build wrote (tools/rift_mines.py SHELL_R, the same rule)

cover.export_tolerance_why: tools/ground.py: round(h) is the exported ground at 99.85% of columns; the rest are one block LOW, at water edges. Under water that block is one block less of seabed than the heightmap promises
cover.natural_seabed_why: one block of the export's own ground is left untouched over the shell, so the sea floor keeps the export's dressing and nothing this build writes is ever the sea floor itself
cover.rule: cover = shell_r + export_tolerance + natural_seabed solid blocks between any cell this build opens and any water, in every direction (Chebyshev). The tool computes it from these three; nothing here states the total

grade.incline_why: past the gatehouse the road drops into an open box-cut falling one block in two until the cover is reached and it goes under a roof (the portal)
grade.max_run_why: the steepest the roofed road may fall where the cover forces it down: one block in six. Elsewhere it falls at the even grade from the portal to its lowest point, one long steady coast, the Cycling Road's downhill
grade.climb_why: the road's last stretch climbs one in one, every rail an ascending powered rail and every step a stair beside it, from its lowest point under the isle's skirt up into the keeper's hall: straight, so the line has no curve and needs no minecraft:rail
grade.quiet_why: no stair within 3 cells of the strip mine's junction or of either end, and a flat bottom of 4 cells: a powered rail cannot meet a stair at a junction, and the stops are on the flat

route.why: ONE straight leg along z1795, west, from the stop in Foothill Gate (its east wall is the buffer) to the stop in Driftmouth Light's keeper's hall (its west wall is the buffer). The owner's point (1455 113 1795) stands inside the gatehouse, on the line

strip_mine.why: the ordinary strip mine: a 3-wide corridor north off the drift, and from it 1-wide, 2-high branches every third block on both sides, two blocks of rock between each pair, so a player walking the branches sees every face. It ends in a small chamber with the miners' barrel

ores.why: the ores the Rift dig camp's faces already carry (data/rift_mines.json veins: copper, gold, lapis), and nothing else: coal, iron, redstone, diamond and emerald ore are spawn conditions (data/spawn_blocks.json: rolycoly, aron, klink, carbink, sableye and more), and a mine is not the place to decide encounters by accident. Exposure rises from the corridor's start to its end and the far branches carry more gold and lapis, so walking further pays; every branch ends on a seam of end_seam ore cells, and hidden_share more lie one block into the walls for anyone who digs

centre.ground_note: built ground: tools/sea_drift.py raises the isle out of the seabed with tools/islet.py's island_top (the Relic Island shape at this radius, crown and seed), so the heightmap carries the seabed and the ground is ours. The centre is set 3 south of the road's axis so that its column is ground, not road: y69 here is the lighthouse pad (pad_y)

island.radius_why: 28, not the first isle's 24: the road climbs one in one from its bottom under the isle's skirt into the keeper's hall, and needs the isle's dry crown along 32 blocks of it. At 24 the climb broke its water cover by up to 6 blocks (tools/sea_drift.py refuses: 'the climb into the isle cannot meet the coast under cover'), measured 2026-10-02; at 28 it holds 4 everywhere. The water here is shallower than at z1586, so each stack's lower Habitat Block (10 over the seabed) stands 1 to 20 under its upper one (4 under the sea, y58): y53 NE, y38 NW, y45 SW and y57 SE, where the two are adjacent
island.skirt_why: islet.py's shape ends at the waterline in a wall 4 under the sea; over 36 blocks of water that would be a pillar, so a talus skirt falls from there to the seabed over 10 more blocks of radius
island.beach_why: a shingle beach, the mine's spoil: sand is a spawn condition (sandygast, palossand: data/spawn_blocks.json), gravel is not
island.pad_why: the ground the lighthouse stands on, levelled over the hall and the tower and 2 round them
island.stacks_why: four sea stacks 51 blocks out on the diagonals, each carrying two of the isle's Habitat Blocks inside its rock: one 4 under the sea for the surface and the upper water, one 10 over the seabed for the deep water and the floor. 72 blocks apart, so no two stacks' spawn boxes (16 each way) overlap; activated blocks do not cancel one another in any case (tools/habitat_blocks.py)

hall.why: the keeper's hall, the road's west gatehouse: the road climbs out of the floor into it, the stop against its west wall, a door south to a path down to the shingle, the tower's door in its north wall

tower.why: a 7-by-7 tower on the hall's north wall, white and red in bands of four (calcite and red terracotta), a stair spiralling round a 3-by-3 stone-brick core lit by glowstone in its faces, to a glazed lantern room at y94 with a gallery round it and a copper cap to y100. The lamp is glowstone, two high: light 15 and no spawn condition (data/spawn_blocks.json names neither glowstone nor glass; the sea lantern is not one either, but this repo swaps it out of ruins for looks, and a lighthouse's lamp reads warm)

waters.level_band_why: reached from the foothill woods (band 21-23) off Route 3, before the third gym, whose cap is 30 (derived/availability.json caps: gym 3 30; docs/mechanics/PROGRESSION_LADDER.md 4.1). One cap band, the shape the western sea's bands take (data/spawns.json marine_zones windward_sea: one gym cap per band): the top of the band is the cap the player holds there, so everything caught is usable
waters.roster_why: cold, strange and old: what lives off a spoil heap in the northern shelf's water. None of Magikarp, Goldeen or Barraskewda (the owner is tired of them: every lake is that), and none of the western sea's deep band (data/spawns.json windward_depths: chinchou is the one shared, as the anchor). Binacle clings to the stacks and the shingle, the one grounded species, so the isle's dry ground is not empty where the blocks cancel the pack's spawns. Rarity buckets and family weights are data/spawns.json `rarity`. Each species' spawnable position is taken from its existing entries in data/spawns.json (tools/position_types.py derived them from the Cobblemon jar), never written here. An evolution whose level is above the band's minimum is listed authored-only (weight 0), the evolution_policy's eligibility rule; the levels are the ones data/spawns.json's eligibility reasons already record. Barbaracle and Clawitzer are left out: no entry in data/spawns.json records their level
waters.shore_why: two more blocks inside the isle's own shore rock, north and south, 4 under the sea, so the water against the beach is the isle's too
waters.why: activated blocks keep up to max_spawns of the pool alive round themselves (data/habitat_blocks.json, the elder nests), and cancel_range 16 cancels the pack's own natural spawns round each block, which is where the Magikarp come from: the open sea here is the pack's inherited pools (STATE: 'the pack's own ocean pools ran there (Magikarp 1-20 and Wishiwashi 1-18)'). Whether an activated block's fixed-area spawner places submerged, surface and seafloor spawns in water is NOT verified: the research reads it as the ordinary position search (docs/research/notes/habitat-nest-perching.md: the spawner is a box round the block) and no one has looked

palette.rail_why: the boosters and the two stops of the rail line (see rail_line). minecraft:rail is a spawn condition (rolycoly, carkol, coalossal) and is used nowhere: the line is straight, so it never turns

rail_line.design: one straight line down the road's centre from a stop in Foothill Gate to a stop in Driftmouth Light's keeper's hall. Every ascending rail (every step of the coast, every rail of the climb) is a powered rail with power; on the flat a powered rail at least every boost_every-th rail; the rest are detector rails, which a cart rides as plain rail and which are no spawn condition. There is no curve, so no minecraft:rail. Each powered rail is powered by its own lever, switched on, two blocks under it, on the ceiling of the rock cell under the rail's bed: the lever strongly powers the bed, the bed powers the rail. The lever is sealed in rock, so nobody sees or flips it. Each stop is an unpowered powered rail against its building's wall (the buffer) with a stone button on the floor beside it: an arriving cart is braked to a stop on it, and a press launches a stationary cart away from the wall. Between each stop and the line is one activator rail, unpowered, so no powered rail is connected to the stop and nothing powers it but its button

physics.edition: Java Edition 1.21.1. The experimental minecart changes of 1.21.2 and later (the minecart_improvements feature, game rule minecartMaxSpeed) do NOT apply
physics.source: the Minecraft Wiki, read 2026-10-02: https://minecraft.wiki/w/Rail (section 'Minecart speeds'), https://minecraft.wiki/w/Powered_Rail, https://minecraft.wiki/w/Activator_Rail, https://minecraft.wiki/w/Minecart
physics.occupied_why: Rail, 'Minecart speeds' table, 'Minecart with entity': 112 rails at full speed initially, then 38 and 26 alternately, each followed by one powered rail, keep full speed. The audit takes the smaller, 26
physics.margin_why: the audit fails any run of more than 26 / 2 = 13 rails between powered rails; boost_every 12 gives at most 11, so the line is boosted at 26/11, more than twice as often as the wiki says full speed needs
physics.climb: Rail: 'The minimum number of powered rails to keep the cart climbing constantly is 3 every 6 blocks'; 'With a rider, a minecart can climb at most 24 blocks before stopping'. Every ascending rail here is powered: 6 in 6, twice the minimum
physics.propagation_why: Powered Rail: 'An activated powered rail also activates any adjacent powered rails it is connected to, up to eight away from the original activation source'. Not relied on (every booster has its own source); it is why the stops are parted from the line by an activator rail
physics.brake: Powered Rail: 'An inactive powered rail reduces the speed of a moving minecart, usually stopping it within one block's distance even on a downward-slanted track'
physics.launch: Powered Rail: an activated powered rail will 'accelerate a non-moving minecart away from a solid opaque block the powered rail is facing'
physics.max_speed: Minecart: 'a predefined speed limit of exactly 8 blocks per second per axis of travel'
physics.activator: Activator Rail: when activated it 'ejects mobs (including players) from minecarts', so no power source and no detector rail is ever next to one
physics.assumed: NOT from a source, to be probed in game (experiments/EXP-050-drift-minecart-line): that an occupied cart arriving at full speed stops on the single stop rail without leaving the line, that a cart holds the climb of one in one for its whole length on powered rails, and that rails placed by setblock in route order settle to the shapes written

rail_line.spawn_policy: none: the line writes no minecraft:rail (the first line's 12 curves and their data/spawn_block_policy.json exception went with the bends); tools/sea_drift_audit.py fails any rail that turns and any spawn condition written

lights.why: a pair of lanterns under the roof over the footpaths every 6 cells, a timber set (basalt posts in the walls, a copper beam in the roof) between each pair, as the dig camp's adit (frames 5, light_every 5): at 8 blocks a second a rider passes a pair of lamps and a set of timbers every three quarters of a second. Light is checked, not assumed: the audit floods block light from every lamp and fails any floor cell under a roof at light 0. There are no vanilla hostiles in this pack (docs/STATE.md, MobsBeGone), so the light is for the ride

rebuild.constraint: a vanilla 1.21.1 minecart is capped at 8 blocks a second on each axis (rail_line physics max_speed), and the first line already ran at the cap. A rail runs along one axis, so a rail route between two ends is at least |dx| + |dz| long: the first line's ends, (1458, 1795) and (345, 1584), give 1,113 + 211 = 1,324, its own length. The trip is shortened only by moving an end, and a straight line needs both ends on one axis
